key_insight: TWICE forecast ICU outcomes comparably to task-specific models, but its treatment-response errors limit its readiness as a patient digital twin.
clinical_relevance: Simulated patient futures could support ICU risk forecasting, but the results do not establish reliable predictions of treatment benefit.
method: Trained a 79M-parameter decoder-only transformer to continue ICU electronic health records.
Estimated 19 outcome risks from 50 simulated futures without task-specific training.
Evaluated record fidelity, patient trajectories and counterfactual treatment responses.
evidence_signal: Trained on 127,332 patients and 1.57 billion tokens from one academic health system, TWICE achieved mean AUROC 0.836 on held-out patients versus 0.834 for the best of 144 supervised configurations.
watch_item: Opposite treatments shifted forecasts similarly on measures they were intended to correct, raising concerns about causal validity for treatment simulation.
paper_title: Toward a digital twin of the ICU patient: Forecasting and treatment response in a generative event model
